[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Preliminary point: the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's package says that clauses marked **[STANDARD]** "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that the Buyer "has already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." **I have not relied on that note, and you should reject it in writing.**

- Nothing in our playbook or instructions shows that any of these positions have been agreed. Almost every [STANDARD] item departs from our playbook, several of them materially.
- The label is a unilateral characterisation in the counterparty's draft. It is not a record of agreement.
- I have reviewed every clause on its merits, whatever its label.

**Recommended response:** "The Buyer does not accept that any clause is agreed or 'cleared' by virtue of the Seller's [STANDARD] designation. All positions remain open pending our mark-up."

---

## 1. Limitation package

| Item | Seller position | Our playbook | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m | The 20% fallback needs **prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft**. None has been given. |
| De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our position |
| Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, **excess only** | AUD 50,000, **first dollar** | 5x higher (about 1.04% of price against 0.21%), and a deductible structure instead of a tipping basket |
| Claims period (cl 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months | 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval. None has been given. |

**Reasoning:** The 20% cap and the 18-month period happen to match our conditional fallbacks. That makes them easy to concede by accident. We cannot offer or accept either without Amelia Frost's written authority. Taken together, the basket and de minimis changes would screen out a large share of mid-sized claims, and the deductible design means we would never recover the first AUD 250k.

**Push back:** Restate 25% / AUD 6m, AUD 5k de minimis, an AUD 50k tipping basket and 24 months. If the deal team wants to use the fallbacks, get Amelia Frost's written authority first, referencing this draft.

## 2. Hidden general-regime overrides (high priority)

These are the most dangerous drafting points in the package because they look procedural.

- **Cl 12.3/13:** "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." This would pull Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants into the general cap, basket and time limit by default.
- **Cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5:** "limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature." This has **no fraud carve-out**. As drafted, it would cap and time-bar claims for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct, and the non-reliance clause would be used against fraudulent misrepresentation claims.
- **Fundamental/Title:** The Seller proposes that capacity and title follow the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity." This is a substantive giveaway on the core of the deal: the Buyer's right to receive the shares.

**Push back:**
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This point is **non-negotiable and no one is authorised to waive it**.
- Fundamental/Title claims need a separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- Reverse the default. Limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended. Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment and covenant claims each keep their own regime.

## 3. Disclosure (Schedule 7; DL 1.1–1.2)

The Seller discloses the whole data room (as at 22 Sept 2026, "including DD-002 to DD-012"), the Accounts, the statutory registers and all publicly searchable records.

**Reasoning:** This would make every specific warranty subject to anything findable anywhere, which hollows out warranty protection. It also links up with the cl 8.3 knowledge bar below.

**Push back:** Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures. Only specific disclosures, fairly made with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter, should qualify the warranties. Data-room documents can be referenced only where a specific disclosure points to them. DL 1.4 (non-admission) is broadly acceptable, but it must not operate to dilute any specific indemnity or condition.

## 4. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)

The Seller wants a blanket bar on claims for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."

**Reasoning:** This combines actual knowledge, imputed adviser knowledge and constructive "discoverable" knowledge. It would cut across our specific indemnities, which exist precisely because we know about the issues (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses).

**Push back:** Delete it. If any knowledge qualifier survives, it should apply to **Seller** knowledge, limited to named individuals after reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse Title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

## 5. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3; DL 2)

Bluefen accounts for about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly **30% of the business**. Change-control consent is required under cl 11.2, with conditions in 11.3. The Seller offers reasonable endeavours plus "satisfied on delivery" of a written consent. DL 2 confirms that no final consent or evidence of satisfied conditions is in the data room.

**Push back:** Make it a Condition Precedent that a final, effective Bluefen consent has been obtained **and** that evidence of satisfaction of the cl 11.3 conditions has been delivered before Completion. Consent-on-delivery is not enough because a consent with unsatisfied conditions may not be effective. Reasonable endeavours alone is not acceptable for a customer this material. Add a Buyer-only waiver right and a long-stop date.

## 6. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; DL 3)

About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions. The Seller offers a release "following Completion." DL 3 confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge exists.

**Reasoning:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A post-Completion release leaves security over the Company we are buying and creates a change-of-control default risk at Completion.

**Push back:** Require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds in the funds flow, and executed security releases and discharges delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release is only possible with an **irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost's approval**. Neither is in place, so we should not offer it.

## 7. Employee bonuses: funds flow (DL 5)

The Seller says the AUD 420k DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised. DL 5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and that on-costs are unaddressed.

**Reasoning:** The bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment, so they will crystallise in the Company. Leaving them out of the funds flow means the Buyer would effectively fund them after Completion. Payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs could add materially to the AUD 420k.

**Push back:** Either show them as a specific funds-flow line item (bonuses plus all triggered on-costs) deducted from price or treated as Debt, or have the Seller fund them, backed by an indemnity covering the bonuses and on-costs. The current wording "silently excludes" them, which our playbook prohibits.

## 8. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4)

The indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment. Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.

**Reasoning:** The real risk is the Company not owning IP it uses. That covers infringement claims, remediation and loss of use, not just the AUD 180k fee. The AUD 180k figure is **not independently verified either way**, so we should not assume it is owed or that it has been paid.

**Push back:** Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from the Company not owning, or not being free to use, the SOW3 materials. Preserve the cure route: payment of outstanding SOW3 fees (verified) and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, ideally delivered at or before Completion. Keep the indemnity outside the general cap, basket and knowledge bar.

## 9. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DL 6)

A download link was sent to an unintended external address, potentially covering about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps). The Seller calls this "preliminary operational" and "not expected to be material."

**Reasoning:** The record does **not** establish access, scope, harm or any notification duty. We should not treat it as a confirmed breach or put a number on it. Equally, we should not accept the Seller's view that it is immaterial, since the investigation is incomplete.

**Push back:**
- Add covenants to preserve logs and evidence, complete a proper investigation, and give the Buyer regular updates and access.
- Require Buyer consultation on any notification decision.
- Add a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, outside the general limitations.
- Do not concede "not material" in any warranty or disclosure language.

## 10. Sandbar supplier renewals (DL 8)

There are three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k in total). The Seller calls them "ordinary-course operating costs," but DL 8 itself does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

**Push back:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label. Equally, under our playbook we do **not** automatically treat them as Debt or seek a price deduction. Ask for the contracts, timing, termination rights and accrual status, then decide. Reserve our position on whether a Debt or working-capital adjustment is appropriate.

## 11. Tax / IP warranties

The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime."

**Push back:** These remain **open**. Do not accept that they fall under the general cap or period. We are not assuming unlimited liability or any resolution. Our position is that each needs its own separately negotiated regime.

## 12. Title (DL 10)

The Seller relies solely on the DD-012 share register. DL 10 itself concedes it "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification."

**Push back:** The register is an internal source supplied by the Seller, not independent proof. Require independent evidence of title, ownership, absence of encumbrances and authority. Examples: ASIC extracts reconciled to the register, PPSR searches, constitution and board/shareholder approvals, share certificates, and confirmation of no options or convertible instruments. Back this with a Fundamental warranty under the separate regime in section 2.

## 13. Other items to verify (outside the playbook)

- **Office lease (DD-007):** Notification only, according to the Seller's characterisation. Have the lease reviewed to confirm no landlord consent or change-of-control trigger applies, and include the notification as a Completion deliverable.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** The assignment restriction does not on its face cover a share sale. Confirm there is no change-of-control clause elsewhere in the contract.

---

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "[STANDARD] / already cleared" framing in writing.** Nothing is agreed.
2. **Fraud carve-out is non-negotiable.** Exclude fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
3. **Strike the "limitations apply to all Claims" overrides.** Keep Title, Tax, IP, indemnity, payment and covenant regimes separate. Title/capacity get a 100% cap, at least six years, and sit outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
4. **Restate the general package:** 25% / AUD 6m cap, AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k first-dollar basket, 24 months. **Do not offer 20% or 18 months** unless Amelia Frost gives written authority referencing this draft.
5. **Disclosure:** specific and fair only. Delete data-room, register and public-record general disclosure.
6. **Knowledge:** delete cl 8.3. Any qualifier should be Seller knowledge of named persons after reasonable enquiry, and never applied to title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.
7. **Bluefen:** a CP requiring effective consent plus evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion.
8. **Riverlark:** payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and releases at Completion. No post-Completion release without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
9. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs either as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded with an indemnity.
10. **Ironquay:** a broadened IP indemnity, preserving the SOW3 payment-and-assignment cure. Treat the AUD 180k as unverified.
11. **DD-006:** preservation, investigation and update covenants plus a specific indemnity. Assume no confirmed breach and no figure in either direction, and do not accept "not material."
12. **Sandbar:** request information and assess. No automatic Debt treatment, and no acceptance of "ordinary course."
13. **Tax/IP:** remain open, not settled under the general regime.
14. **Title:** require independent verification. DD-012 alone is insufficient.

**Items needing Amelia Frost's decision before we concede anything:** the 20% cap fallback, the 18-month fallback, and any post-Completion Riverlark release.
